key_insight: A simulator-trained inverse map lets Bayesian optimization search a low-dimensional representation while preserving the original problem geometry through its Gaussian process kernel.
engineering_relevance: The approach can reduce costly black-box evaluations when an approximate mechanistic simulator is available.
method: Train an inverse map offline from simulator parameters to predicted optimal decisions.
Run Bayesian optimization over the learned representation using a geometry-aware Gaussian process kernel.
Analyze approximation bias and information gain, and derive an intrinsic-dimension-dependent regret rate under additional assumptions.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations of personalized Parkinson’s drug dosing show improved optimization performance, including under simulator misspecification; no clinical evaluation is reported in the abstract.
watch_item: Restricting search to the learned representation can introduce approximation bias and exclude better solutions outside it.
paper_title: Bayesian optimization on amortized search space
